title: Line Follower Robot
tagline: An autonomous PID-controlled robot that follows a black line at speed.
problem: I wanted to build a fully autonomous robot that could follow a predefined path reliably — something that actually moves at speed without constantly overcorrecting. The classic bang-bang control felt clunky. I wanted smooth, responsive motion.

timeline.title: Concept & Planning
timeline.desc: Chose PID over bang-bang. Sketched chassis layout. Sourced components.

timeline.title: Hardware Assembly
timeline.desc: Cut PVC chassis. Mounted motors and caster. Wired motor driver to Arduino.

timeline.title: Sensor Calibration
timeline.desc: Wrote calibration routine. Found sensor 3 was giving noisy readings — resoldered joint.

timeline.title: PID Tuning
timeline.desc: Manually tuned Kp, Ki, Kd. Spent 6 hours on this. Kd was the game changer.

timeline.title: Testing & Refinement
timeline.desc: Track testing. Added weight balancing to the front. Final performance: 0.8m/s on curves.

failures: Sensor 3 noisy output — caused by cold solder joint. Re-soldered fixed it.
Oscillation at high speed — Kd was too low. Increased from 0.1 to 0.8.
Battery sag causing erratic behavior — added capacitor across motor power rails.
Chassis flex at speed — added cross-brace from spare PVC strip.

results.top_speed: 0.8 m/s on curves, 1.1 m/s on straights
